## Jira-side assessment + bridge re-enable checklist (2026-09-06 ~01:00Z)

Duplicate remediation is COMPLETE (386/386, verified independently — see
`anarchic-princely-raven`). Bridge remains DISABLED. Numbers below are measured, and the
first-pass write plan was verified against **live Jira**, not against the stored baselines.

### Where the two sides stand
- Bridge last mirrored **2026-09-05T14:33:31Z** (`last-pass.json`, `outcome: success`).
  Scheduled runs 15:00-19:00Z never fired; workflow set `disabled_manually` at 19:19:35Z.
  Effective blackout ~10.5 h.
- Jira **REB**: 5349 issues — 4527 Done, 822 not-Done. Bindings: 5333.
- **No durable bridge pause is set** (`refs/reconciler/pause` absent; only
  `refs/reconciler/last-pass` exists). The GitHub workflow disable is the ONLY gate.

### First-pass write plan — 403 transitions (verified live, not from baselines)
| change | count |
|---|---|
| To Do -> Done | 389 |
| In Progress -> Done | 9 |
| **Done -> To Do (UNWANTED reopens)** | **3** |
| To Do -> In Progress | 1 |
| Done -> (archived ticket, REB-4603) | 1 |

398 of these are closes; ~386 are this incident's duplicates, the rest ordinary work closed
during the blackout.

**A raw-drift scan overstates this badly.** 510 bindings carry `baseline.status = null` and
naively read as "needs Done". All 510 were checked live and are **already Done** — zero
transitions. Anyone sizing this from `bindings.json` alone will see ~775 and panic.

### Capacity / ceiling
- Reads paginate at 100/page (`fetch_paging.py`) — REB's 5349 issues are NOT exposed to
  Jira's 5000-row `maxResults` ceiling. Inbound GETs are rotation-budgeted
  (`get_rotation.json`). No query-ceiling risk.
- Writes are the risk. acli is serial at ~4 s/issue, so 403 transitions is ~27 min of pure
  write time **on top of** normal pass work. Recent passes already ran 6-32 min at near-zero
  drift. The workflow `timeout-minutes` is **60**, and **commit-back only persists on a
  COMPLETED pass** — so a `live` first pass can plausibly time out, persist NOTHING, and
  re-attempt the same 403 every hour indefinitely.
- Mitigation is already built in: `bootstrap-throttle` = `bridge sync --max-changes 100`.
  Four throttled passes drain the backlog, each well inside the timeout, each committing back.

Profile ladder (`src/rebar/_bridge_runner.py`):
`dry-run`/`reconcile-check` -> `bridge preview` (0 writes) | `bootstrap-strict` -> `--max-changes 10`
| `bootstrap-throttle` -> `--max-changes 100` | `live` -> uncapped.

### Would this cause a second incident?
Two things must be settled first.
1. **The fix has NOT landed.** Gerrit change **2688** ("Refuse force_new_store inside a linked
   worktree") is `NEW`: `Verified +1`, **no LLM-Review vote**. The leak vector is still open on
   main. The bridge does not create duplicates, but it **amplifies** them: with the bridge on,
   the next tier-2 eval run turns fresh rebar duplicates into real new **Jira issues**. That is
   a strictly worse blast radius than the incident just cleaned up.
2. **3 unwanted reopens.** REB-806/807/808 are `Done` in Jira but `open` in rebar because
   their rebar tickets are synthetic `code_review` test fixtures
   (`rebar~main~Iabc @ rev1`, `~Igap @ rev-gap`, `~Imerge @ mrev`; a 4th, 34f9, is unbound).
   The first pass will reopen all three.

### Re-enable checklist (OPERATOR-GATED — not performed)
Preconditions
1. Change **2688** has `LLM-Review +1` and is **submitted/merged**. Do not re-enable before
   this; the bridge is the amplifier, not the cause.
2. Confirm no tier-2 / plan-replay eval is running or scheduled against the live store.
3. Decide on REB-806/807/808: close the three synthetic `code_review` tickets in rebar
   (so the pass sees Done->Done no-ops), or accept three reopens. Same call for unbound
   34f9-add3-5ee5-4a83.
4. Re-confirm the count immediately before enabling (it drifts as work lands):
   expect ~403 (~398 closes).

Sequence
```
# 1. Dry run FIRST — computes the mutation set, applies none.
gh workflow run reconcile-bridge.yml --field mode=dry-run
gh run watch $(gh run list --workflow reconcile-bridge.yml --limit 1 --json databaseId -q '.[0].databaseId')

# 2. Compare the dry-run manifest against the expected ~403 / ~398-close shape.
#    Then ONE throttled pass (max 100 changes):
gh workflow run reconcile-bridge.yml --field mode=bootstrap-throttle

# 3. Inspect, repeat step 2 until the backlog is drained (~4 passes).

# 4. Only then restore the hourly schedule:
gh workflow enable reconcile-bridge.yml
```

Watch on the first pass
- Change count in the manifest: must be ~403, and **~398 of them closes**.
- **Any CREATE of a new Jira issue.** Steady state here is transitions only; a create means
  an unbound local ticket appeared. Investigate before continuing.
- Pass duration vs the 60-min `timeout-minutes`.
- `last-pass.json` `outcome: success` and `completed_at` advancing — commit-back only
  persists on a completed pass.
- REB-806/807/808 behaviour matches the decision in precondition 3.

ABORT SIGNALS — `gh workflow disable reconcile-bridge.yml` immediately
- The manifest proposes **more than ~450 changes**, or **any** issue CREATE.
- Jira REB total rises above 5349 (+ any issues legitimately created since).
- A pass hits the 60-min timeout (nothing persists; it will loop).
- Any new same-title collision group appears in rebar — the leak has re-fired.
- `bridge fsck` reports `binding_drift` or `store_integrity` problems.

### Housekeeping
`JIRA_API_TOKEN` (Atlassian Cloud, user joeoakhart@navapbc.com) is exported in the operator's
local shell and was inadvertently echoed into an agent session transcript during this
investigation. No external transmission, but **rotate it** as a precaution.
